hello.speaker: envoy
hello.text: The archlord offers an easier ending. Seris may transfer the service to her surviving bloodline. Or Rowan may be released in exchange for a new soul. There are precedents for both. Why trouble yourselves with the foundations of a law when you could purchase an exception?

choices.text: Reject both substitutions and challenge the claims.
Ask why he calls an unsigned soul a debt.

law.speaker: envoy
law.text: “Continuity,” he says. “Civilisation depends on obligations surviving the people who make them.” Seris answers: “A bridge can be inherited. So can its upkeep. A person is not a bridge.” The envoy does not answer her. He asks whether you brought the original grant.

challenge.speaker: envoy
challenge.text: Place the original grant, the counterseal, and a freely offered account before the court.

missing.speaker: envoy
missing.text: Your case is incomplete. The counterseal is in the Counting House, the original grant in the family manor, and a free witness must speak from sanctuary. Charm cannot create valid testimony. The court will hear you when the record is complete.

fight.speaker: envoy
fight.text: “My servants will show you the cost of impatience.” These are mortal retainers, not the archlord himself. Defeating them will not cancel a contract.

verdict.text: The counterseal exposes the forged rider. Mara’s free testimony connects the collections to the unlawful claim. The tribunal annuls the archlord’s lien and Seris’s delegated bond together, with no substitution and no gap in protection. Seris’s inherited service is void. Rowan’s soul remains his own. At sanctuary, use the fire to speak with Rowan about what comes next.

choices.text: Return to Rowan at the sanctuary.

after.speaker: envoy
after.text: The envoy has gone. The court’s decision covers these claims; it does not free every soul in the vault. The register remains a promise of work, not a declaration that the work is finished.
